title: Bind the baseline and publish the product contract
deliverables: Verify the archive and per-file hashes; create the working branch from the 244-file exported tree.
Install the normative documentation and status ledger without describing target features as already shipped.
Inventory all references to removed IDs and known current placement/default statements.
done_when: Baseline identity is recorded; no application code is imported wholesale from the alternate package.
Product contract and current implementation facts are visibly distinguished.

title: Remove obsolete IDs and retain supported product scope
deliverables: Remove Happy/Happy Remote/Gemini CLI and all Happy backend fields and flags.
Fold Cowork capability settings into claude-desktop rather than retaining cowork-dispatch.
Retain claude-desktop and antigravity-remote; replace obsolete reasons only when their actual implementation gates are satisfied.
Remove obsolete family checks and release-monitor references; preserve every unrelated component and user data directory.
Keep nano/tmux and existing base recovery tools unconditionally installed through catalog cleanup and every preset.
done_when: Deleted IDs fail with actionable errors, without automatic account migration or data deletion.
No executable Happy/Gemini configuration path remains; historic migration notes are explicitly scoped.

title: Add pinned application and helper closures
deliverables: Add independently held Happier, Hermes, Pi and OMP families and components.
Audit current package definitions; package missing Happier runtime/bridges declaratively rather than invoking its network installer.
Select Hermes extras without automatically installing browser/CUA/speech/local-model features.
Map unique commands and remove or privately contain ambiguous package aliases such as Grok agent; test all-curated coexistence.
Record platform/CPU requirements and client-managed-code exceptions.
done_when: Both target architectures evaluate or produce an explicit component-specific unsupported result before destructive installation.
Pinned closures and lock diff contain only intended family/helper changes; self-updaters cannot replace Assbox-managed binaries.

title: Refresh native desktop packaging and prerequisites
deliverables: Identify exact native ChatGPT/Claude source and versions; prefer supported official Linux artifacts where compatible.
Package required libraries, launchers, portals and Secret Service integration on NixOS.

Audit helper downloads and supported managed settings independently of distro install instructions. Identify which policy keys/delivery paths actually apply to each Linux client/build/account; browser policy alone is not a universal local-agent disable switch, and macOS/Windows MDM documentation is not proof of Linux enforcement.

Inventory local Cowork QEMU/firmware/virtiofs/vsock prerequisites only for selected eligible post-6-October account/build modes. Ordinary native chat/cloud must not enable a VM or require device privileges; disclose unavoidable inert helper code bundled by the native app.
done_when: App installation/launch is tested independently from coding/Cowork isolation qualification.
Native requirements and actual package provenance appear in the release support record.

title: Implement pure preset resolution and policy
deliverables: Define four purpose categories and concrete preset IDs as data, with no command recipes.
Resolve presets into explicit components, worker selection, presentation, access defaults and consent requirements.
Persist informational purpose/preset/version provenance in ordinary Nix; runtime security is derived from concrete settings.
Add deterministic validation for exclusions, dependencies, architecture, lack of KVM, removed IDs and unsupported feature combinations.
Keep raw component defaults off; prevent later bundle updates from changing installed selection.
Define minimal coder-codex-ssh and separate Claude relay/SSH presets; grouped Cursor, Antigravity and OpenCode native choices; no automatic Codex relay daemon for SSH.

Represent native kiosk localExecution=none as requested policy, not asserted capability. Consume typed shell-observed facts plus release-qualified policy contracts; return verified, pending, unsupported, ineffective or stale/conflicting findings per app/feature. No-worker activation requires verified enforcement. Keep callbacks and account secrets out of the pure core.

Represent independent ChatGPT Codex/Work/local-bridge observations in native-policy resolution. A missing, newly exposed or ineffective locally acting surface blocks the affected native activation; one disabled entitlement never supplies evidence for another surface.
done_when: Resolver is pure, deterministic and idempotent; no filesystem/process/network callbacks enter functional core.
Nix and Rust agree on resolved placement and errors; changing a label cannot bypass an assertion.
Unknown facts do not resolve to an active native kiosk; Custom and generated settings cannot bypass required policy. Informational role selection is not enforcement evidence.

title: Build the category-first installer and explicit reconfiguration
deliverables: Present Assistant/Coder/Kiosk/Custom before low-level arrangement choices.
Implement branch menus, independent agent selection, private access choices and capability/resource summary.
Keep the prepared-storage, release verification and pre-write authorization flow intact.
Add `assbox configure` to reuse the same selection/resolution path for a proposed existing-machine change; show a diff and require explicit apply, preserving local.nix.
Never convert standalone/managed-worker persistent state as a routine profile switch. Require a separate explicit export/migration procedure.
Expose installed/authenticated/integration-maturity/qualification separately in selection summaries. Show actual transport and controller/tool-execution locations.
Make Codex-over-SSH directly discoverable in Coder and explain the external macOS/Parallels topology; keep experimental direct relay in Advanced.

Implement the Kiosk policy-gate screen and fail-closed transitions: retain unknown/failed apps inactive, offer only separately qualified protected/remote or explicit web alternatives, and allow Back/deselection. Unknown account checks can be deferred into staged setup but cannot authorize unrestricted launch or force authentication during read-only browsing.
done_when: Golden terminal transcripts cover every branch, backtracking, consent refusal, deselection and cancellation before writes.
Reconfiguration builds/validates before publication and reports custom local overrides rather than overwriting them.

Golden transcripts cover verified, pending, unavailable, ineffective and stale policy, mixed-app outcomes, failed alternative preflight, Back and cancellation. No implicit worker/web selection or weakened local execution occurs.

title: Extend the execution network boundary to standalone
deliverables: Implement root-owned workload egress policy that covers all processes of the execution UID, including SSH shells and user-service children.
Default internet-only; enforce IPv4/IPv6 LAN, overlay, link-local, local-broker and metadata restrictions with reviewed resolver/loopback exceptions.
Allow replies to authorized inbound connections without granting new outbound peer access.
Define least-privilege explicit private exceptions and clearly broader normal/offline modes.
Install fail-closed rules before execution becomes available; preserve administration/recovery independently.
done_when: Adversarial tests cover user namespaces, helper proxies, overlay routes, DNS/rebinding, reboot/reload and failed ruleset installation.
No claim of internet exfiltration prevention or hostile-root containment is made.

title: Make Tailscale the guided default without automatic enrollment
deliverables: Retain the existing tailscale.enable meaning: install/support tailscaled, not authenticate into a tailnet. Guided defaults enable support; raw module default remains off.
Keep root-only enrollment/control, Tailscale SSH off, route acceptance off, no subnet/exit-node advertising and no Funnel default.
Add root-owned approved Serve mappings for explicitly selected dashboards; do not grant the agent Tailscale operator rights.
Make HTTPS consent, application auth, grants and enrollment visible steps; preserve recovery SSH as an independently keyed role.
Remove stale Serve exposure on disable before stopping the backend; do not reset unrelated owner-managed mappings.

For Hermes recommended exposure, configure an exact non-loopback HTTPS public_url while retaining loopback backend binding and native authentication. Verify this behavior on the selected release; do not infer it from listener reachability.

Offer tunnel-only Hermes access only as an explicitly consented Advanced policy exception, never a fallback from broken native authentication; preserve narrow tailnet/SSH access and do not expose publicly.
done_when: An unpaired installed system is not joined or publishing applications.
Happier works without Tailscale; authorized tailnet access works without giving workloads broad peer access.

title: Generalize existing service onboarding only as needed
deliverables: Reuse configuration-bound onboarding markers, private diagnostics and user-manager supervision.
Define staged, setup-required, ready, temporarily unavailable, auth-required, config-error, disabled and retired observations.

Inspect the supported foreground/runtime or exported user-service contract; Nix supplies one reproducible supervisor, not a wrapper around a service installer or daemonizer. Distinguish intentional stop, permanent refusal and transient provider failure.
Gate consent by relevant configuration and runtime/permission contract, not just a mutable unchecked marker.
Ensure explicit stop/disable is durable across boot and no provider-owned service resurrects it.
done_when: Lifecycle ownership is singular; no token appears in normal journal/argv/Nix store.
Missing credentials are not an OS boot failure; diagnostics are bounded and actionable.

title: Integrate Happier and its selected agent bridges
deliverables: Provide happier and happier-daemon selections. Inspect the pinned supported user-systemd unit (including a supported dry-run/export where available), declare its equivalent with exact Nix paths and one supervisor; pairing must not create a competing service or updater.
Configure hosted relay default and a self-hosted endpoint override, supported E2EE enforcement, local provider auth and no automatic external-machine/account-wide imports.
Map Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok and Antigravity adapters to exact pinned paths; inspect Antigravity bridge/auth separately.
Keep Pi/OMP usable as CLIs; enable only verified upstream adapters or Custom ACP configuration.
Test normal approval/cancel/resume behavior without creating an Assbox scheduler.
Display dated upstream maturity per agent adapter and separate Assbox qualification. OMP CLI availability is not proof of a built-in Happier backend.

Use the pinned upstream headless auth login --no-open --method web flow as the normal no-browser/no-TTY setup. Offer owner-initiated auth pair-remote --ssh only from an already authenticated trusted client, after verifying the target host key, execution user and selected server/account scope. Do not require incoming SSH or Tailscale for the local URL flow.

Inspect pairing side effects on the selected releases: credential writes, runtime resolution, service creation/start, updater and autostart. Keep credentials private to the execution identity and redact URLs/codes/tokens including JSON diagnostics. A pair command that cannot preserve single-owner managed lifecycle must be unavailable; use the explicitly selected URL flow instead, not an extra wrapper daemon or copied HOME.
done_when: Real remote Codex and Claude sessions run on the intended execution machine.
Installed/deselected agent behavior and bridge provisioning match the selected closure and disclosure.

Every enabled pairing path has expiry/cancel/retry/revocation evidence, exact machine/account mapping, no unrelated credential imports, and no competing service; an unsupported SSH pairing path reports its exact blocker without blocking a separately qualified URL flow. Package install and preset browsing remain unauthenticated.

title: Refresh OpenClaw as an Assistant integration
deliverables: Reuse Gateway lifecycle and private dashboard profile; make channel pairing and tool policy explicit.
Pin selected ACP/native plugins and bridges, including exact executable paths; no ad-hoc npx/latest bootstrap in normal supported flows.
Configure loopback authenticated UI and optional root-managed Serve; retain advanced node capabilities and explicit private-node egress exceptions.
Separate model credentials from external CLI subscription credentials.
Retain supported upstream automations; no universal global agent orchestration layer.
done_when: Authorized channel request and private UI task succeed; unknown senders/unauthenticated clients fail.
Delegation, cancellation and gateway restart behavior are exercised for selected agents.

title: Add Hermes as an Assistant integration
deliverables: Add hermes CLI, hermes-gateway and independent hermes-dashboard options from one family.
Run `hermes gateway` in foreground; use an explicit persistent HERMES_HOME with no root/sudo or default Docker socket.
Reuse upstream model setup, messaging allowlists/pairing and bundled delegation skills; preserve selected provider identity/state across restarts.
Offer the dashboard as a separate opt-in access choice; configure exact public URL, Host/Origin, trusted proxy and native auth semantics for loopback+Serve.
Keep application memory, skills, schedules and user-auth data mutable/persistent while the managed runtime remains pinned.
Treat browser/CUA/voice/model helper installation as capability-dependent packaging, not automatic upstream PM actions.

Set dashboard.public_url or HERMES_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_URL to the exact non-loopback HTTPS endpoint; verify documented auth-required/fail-closed behavior with a loopback backend. Secure-cookie and trusted-proxy behavior must be established, not inferred from public_url.

Keep the recommended app-authenticated route unavailable if that pinned behavior is absent; any Advanced tunnel-only exception must have explicit consent and accurately state that the tunnel is its only user-facing gate.
done_when: Gateway messaging and the recommended app-authenticated dashboard are each authorized and actually usable, including WebSockets. An explicitly selected tunnel-only dashboard has separate access evidence and no app-auth claim.
Unknown-sender, update-command, restart, replay and state-recovery tests pass for the chosen release.
Authenticated browser and terminal WebSockets work through Serve, while unauthenticated and forged-header requests fail on protected routes; missing auth configuration fails closed.

title: Integrate provider-native Coder routes and separately gate experiments
deliverables: Keep native Claude Remote, Cursor worker, OpenCode server, VS Code tunnel and OpenClaw node independently selectable.
Replace the Antigravity research blocker with a tested declarative runtime adapter; `agy remote-control start` is not used blindly as a forever-running service command.
Pin actual commands and relevant auth modes; native help commands that require login are not treated as offline build smoke tests.
Preserve independent capability and exposure defaults.

Expose Claude relay, Cursor My Machines, Antigravity Remote and OpenCode authenticated private web/server through purpose-first presets over existing components. Keep their lifecycles and credentials separate.
Document Cursor cloud agent loop versus local tool execution and cloud HTTP/SSE MCP versus local stdio MCP; no claim of universal local execution.

Evaluate experimental codex remote-control foreground/start/stop/pair against the pinned CLI and actual supported clients. If a supported contract exists, add an explicitly experimental codex-remote service and acceptance path; otherwise record the concrete blocker, not guessed flags or a substitute route.

Direct Codex relay enrollment is independent of Desktop SSH, shares no assumed session/credential semantics, and requires expiry/revocation, cancellation, listener and duplicate-supervisor checks. No public app-server port.
done_when: No second daemon is installed; long-lived modes survive logout/boot and stop cleanly.
Each provider path has its own evidence instead of borrowing Happier success.

title: Implement native chat/cloud and protected coding kiosks
deliverables: Provide ChatGPT/Claude selection and physical X11/Openbox defaults; keep optional Wayland for separately qualified combinations.

Request native kiosk localExecution=none, but activate only after exact app/platform/account policy is proven applicable and effectively applied. Selected protected local Code reuses one worker with necessary tools, under its own no-fallback and exact-client gate. Neither KVM nor a worker makes an otherwise unsafe controller safe.
Implement effective Claude Desktop managed SSH settings and local-Code disabling; test resume/fallback/preview/plugin/connector paths separately.
Do not replace controllerAllowed=false with an unconditional allow. Add handwritten feature assertions tied to the qualified native-kiosk profile.
Provide distinct web launchers using protected browser profiles as an explicit no-worker chat/cloud alternative.
Keep normal keyring behavior and clearly explain auto-login does not guarantee unlocked secrets after reboot.

Implement the same native policy gate in setup, launch, reconfiguration and update/rollback activation. Bind evidence to app/helper builds, OS/platform, authentication/workspace scope, feature set and effective policy digest. Do not trust execution-writable readiness markers. A changed or missing contract keeps affected capability inactive until valid observations are available; any safe login/bootstrap path must itself be qualified.

Qualify Linux ChatGPT Desktop -> managed-worker SSH independently from macOS external Desktop and phone->Mac->SSH. Do not infer Linux mobile Remote-host support from Linux GUI availability or generic SSH docs. Keep other independently qualified kiosk apps/routes usable.

Implement the ChatGPT surface contract in specifications/SECURITY_AND_LIFECYCLE.md: Codex Local, Work Local, Work Cloud local-computer access, cloud-only Work/Codex, browser/computer control and local plugins/MCP/helpers have separate placement and policy observations. Test independent enablement, account changes, new/resumed tasks and helper entry points. Workspace entitlement is not a machine-specific deny rule.

Keep Work execution bridges to the protected controller blocked under both no-local-execution and protected-Code presets. A worker alone does not route Work into that worker. Qualify any selected cloud continuation independently, including new-turn loss/recovery of a local computer and differences from Codex SSH/Remote; never imply local Nix/network/enterprise restrictions govern the cloud executor.
done_when: Ordinary native chat/cloud operates without an Assbox guest when its no-local-execution policy is enforceable; selected local Code executes in the worker without controller fallback.
GUI login/close/reopen, keyring lock, session crash and reboot recover without leaking desktop credentials to execution.
Native account/build/policy changes cannot reuse stale activation evidence. Missing native enforcement has an actionable blocked result, not a bypass, automatic local fallback or OS boot failure.

No ChatGPT surface can inherit a false local-execution pass from another surface. Selected cloud-only tasks remain distinguishable from local-capable Work, and Codex SSH success grants no authority to Work or controller helpers.

title: Implement post-6-October Cowork topology and conditional local modes
deliverables: Use deployment floor 2026-10-06. For new Pro/Max tasks expect the documented cloud Cowork path; do not implement pre-transition local-task migration or advertise an Only on your computer control for those tasks.
Detect and record actual entitlement, app version, observed execution topology and feature policies during onboarding. An unexpected rollout or mode must not silently gain local execution.

Qualify cloud Cowork/Dispatch plus explicitly selected local folders, browser bridges and connectors independently of Code SSH. Explain provider-side copies/retention and dependence on an open/connected Desktop bridge.

Only when a selected account/build actually offers local Cowork, implement the separate provider-VM requirements for devices, firmware/helpers, shares, lifecycle, storage and resources. This conditional gate is not a prerequisite for ordinary Claude kiosk support.
Do not redirect Cowork by analogy with SSH Code, grant blanket workload KVM privileges or impose another VM on the external-Codex Parallels profile.
done_when: Ordinary Pro/Max cloud operation has independent evidence and no unintended local-VM dependency.
Eligible local modes remain unavailable until their own qualification passes; inapplicability is documented with account/build evidence rather than counted as a passed VM test.

title: Implement optional browser and virtual desktop support
deliverables: Provide selected browser/X11 dependencies without coupling physical presentation to agent capability.
Adapt Cursor/OpenClaw to provider-managed headless desktops; scrub inherited DISPLAY/Wayland/DBus/Xauthority rather than selecting physical :0.
Provide a small provider-specific isolated-display resource unit for OMP/Hermes only where their pinned tools need one; do not add a task scheduler or new computer-use API.
Keep private browser profiles, browser sandbox, ephemeral display credentials and authenticated optional viewing.
Set a one-active-desktop default; prevent collisions, leaks after teardown and fallback to an unrelated RFB listener.

Maintain exact Linux browser/desktop support rows and native fixtures for each selected provider path. Prefer a qualified upstream-owned Hermes Bot Screen when the pin includes it; a minimal display resource wrapper is only for a pinned path needing an existing display. Do not infer Wayland behavior from X11 success or generic upstream binary limitations from a differently compiled Nix package.
done_when: A headless guest/host without GPU or monitor completes screenshot/input/browser fixtures.
Controller display, keyring and unrelated browser sessions remain inaccessible from the managed worker route.

title: Port canonical identity hardening without storage regressions
deliverables: Port bounded Ed25519 structure parsing, noninteractive private-key validation and whole-key-set validation before side effects.
Validate ownership, group, modes, links, sizes and persistent-state consistency; fail closed on canonical damage and regenerate only verified derived artifacts.
Preserve exact home/overlay 0600 policy, seed chmod under restrictive umask, sparse disk allocation and QEMU werror/rerror stop behavior.
Treat absent home with evidence of operation as damage. Preserve create-only infrastructure metadata rules.
Retain real OpenSSH tests including accumulated wildcard/include identities/certificates/forwardings; do not claim ordinary user SSH config is completely audited.
done_when: Behavioral permission/storage regressions remain green alongside added adversarial identity tests.
Damaged state is unchanged on refusal; no identity rotation occurs beside preserved state.

title: Extend release-family and feature qualification wiring
deliverables: Wire new/removed families through lock handling, generation, checks and release monitoring.
Add profile/composition fixtures without an exhaustive impossible cross-product.
Include exact helper/protocol versions, runtime-code exceptions and feature evidence in release records.
Preserve authenticated publication/admission authority and numeric owner/repository ID provisioning gates.
Require no hidden latest/network install in ordinary image activation; distinguish runtime model traffic from dependency downloads.
done_when: Catalog, generated Rust, family set, lock graph, CI and monitor agree.
Release records cannot label an unrun authenticated feature as qualified.

title: Complete lifecycle, resource and state integration
deliverables: Apply resource accounting to the selected stack including native GUI, provider guest and optional virtual desktops.
Keep liveness local/non-billable; separate network/auth/provider quota issues from OS boot acceptance.
Preserve pinned service restart and retirement behavior through scheduled OS maintenance.
Document and exercise application DB migration/backups/rollback limits.
Do not automatically reissue in-flight tool actions after restart; verify upstream recovery semantics.
done_when: Disabling/removing services leaves no public/private exposure or orphan daemon, while preserving explicitly retained data.
Low-memory/disk-pressure/outage states are bounded and diagnosable.

title: Refresh every affected document and remove conflicting authorities
deliverables: Apply the documentation map and ready-to-integrate product documents.
Rewrite operational examples against implemented settings/commands; retire duplicate proposal language and scope worker docs to managed-worker deployments.
Generate preset/catalog tables from the same reviewed data as the installer.
Attach versioned evidence and explicit statuses to provider capability statements; link dated research separately from stable strategy.
Add documentation checks for stale removed IDs, unsafe examples, broken links and mismatched defaults.

Add a normative Coder-route guide and refresh docs/parallels.md with macOS external-controller responsibilities, exact SSH runtime behavior, guest egress, native versus experimental routes and no-worker native kiosk policy.
Remove all pre-6-October Cowork migration requirements and present local provider VMs as entitlement-dependent; preserve cloud bridge authority warnings.

Publish separate upstream-evidence and Assbox-qualification columns for Mac SSH, phone->Mac->SSH, Linux Desktop->managed-worker SSH and experimental direct relay. Generate no-worker policy and minimal Codex/Tailscale wording consistently across installer, acceptance and operations.

Integrate docs/product/linux-computer-use-support.md as dated evidence, with browser versus screen control, native product versus alternative harness, helper/build prerequisites and Assbox test status separated. Generate it from the planning evidence data; maintain it in the repository with release evidence, not by fetching live websites at boot.

Document independent ChatGPT Work/Codex/local-computer access controls and cloud continuation authority. Link the detailed control inventory from kiosk and external-controller instructions. Add Happier upstream pairing guidance with exact machine roles, redaction and single-supervisor requirements; do not invent an Assbox pairing protocol.
done_when: A reader can determine where execution, credentials and graphical control live for every preset without reading chat history.
No contradictory global claims about headless-only use, all-components-off guided defaults, worker ubiquity or proven Claude token scope remain.
The dated Linux matrix has valid source/date/path references and cannot be mistaken for an Assbox pass; current pairing and per-surface kiosk policy are understandable without chat history.

title: Execute static and native system qualification
deliverables: Run all real Rust, generated-metadata, Nix evaluation/build, native ISO/OpenSSH, VM lifecycle and security gates.
Use exact selected package versions and architecture; report unavailable prerequisites as not run, not pass.
Exercise installation/reconfiguration failure injection and ensure application changes do not bypass worker publication/admission.
done_when: All required automated gates have recorded commands and evidence for the release candidate.
Failures are repaired in code/tests rather than removing gates.

title: Execute authenticated feature and hardware acceptance
deliverables: Use sacrificial identities for credential-boundary probes; use intended subscription/auth modes for normal remote workflows.
Test top-level remote Codex/Claude plus Antigravity/Cursor/Grok delegation via actual selected frontend paths.
Exercise native kiosk, Cowork, headless browser/desktop, remote viewing, revocation and disable behavior independently.
Run reference old x86 hardware and generic ARM VM acceptance, including CPU instructions, memory and power/reboot behavior.
Record exactly which combinations are qualified without calling a default bundle universally equivalent across frontends.

Run the external macOS ChatGPT Desktop -> standalone Parallels guest Codex acceptance path on each advertised CPU architecture. Record client and VM versions, SSH resolved configuration, guest-only canaries, host sharing controls, sleep/reconnect and mobile coordinator dependencies.
Treat experimental CLI Codex relay, Claude relay/SSH and native provider routes as separate client/auth/lifecycle evidence rows, never borrow another route's pass.

Record an independent exact Linux ChatGPT Desktop/worker route result and a separate Linux-as-mobile-Remote-host result when advertised. Mac evidence never substitutes; blocked Linux paths do not veto independently qualified external-Mac or other native-app paths.
done_when: Advertised profile/capability/hardware support is backed by dated reproducible evidence.
Engineering complete and empirical qualification complete remain distinct status fields.

title: Implement external Desktop SSH Coder and Parallels reference path
deliverables: Resolve coder-codex-ssh to standalone Codex and deliberate workload OpenSSH as its only Coder-specific runtime/access components. Keep common Assbox services and explicitly selected Tailscale support. No guest Desktop, inner worker, persistent public app-server service or separately provisioned direct relay.

Make the exact selected Codex command available in the remote login shell. Document guest-side authentication, concrete SSH Host aliases, independent workload keys and trusted-console host-key verification.

Verify the app-started app-server lifetime and any needed SSH channels/forwarding against the selected client; reject incidental identity/certificate/forward accumulation without assuming a blanket forwarding ban is compatible.
Provide Claude Desktop SSH as a separate minimal provider route. Qualify its automatic remote helper provisioning or a supported pin override; do not assume it uses the preinstalled CLI unchanged.

Codify the Mac/Parallels reference topology: matching CPU architecture, no nested virtualization requirement, repositories/credentials in guest, unnecessary host sharing disabled, and independently tested guest execution-egress policy.

Document owner-managed Mac/hypervisor actions separately from Assbox capabilities. Mac-to-guest SSH replies must work while unauthorized guest-initiated access to the Mac/private peers remains blocked.

Implement reproducible canary/disconnect/reconnect acceptance fixtures; test explicit handoff separately from forbidden silent host fallback and document Mac availability for mobile relay coordination.

Test both the guided Tailscale-selected, unenrolled configuration and an explicitly deselected configuration over a reviewed local Mac/guest route. The latter contains no Tailscale runtime/service dependency and performs an actual Desktop SSH task without overlay enrollment.

Label macOS Desktop->SSH and phone->Mac->SSH as upstream-documented topologies awaiting Assbox/Parallels acceptance. Keep exact Linux client and Linux Remote-coordinator qualification in distinct evidence rows; do not change the default Coder route to the experimental CLI relay.
done_when: The exact supported macOS app launches and controls guest Codex over SSH with no extra Assbox VM or public RPC listener.

Guest-only file/process checks, private-network denial, reboot/suspend/reconnect and optional mobile continuation have route-specific evidence. Unobserved client or platform combinations remain unqualified.
